_comment: The b16-ft head: a 16-way linear probe on the crop-jitter fine-tuned BioCLIP B/16
(scratch/2026-10-05-cropjitter-ft/ckpt/A2a_best_acc.pt, epoch 6), replacing the zero-shot
text head of public/text_embeds_b16.json. Same FORMAT as that file; four things differ and
each is asserted in tests/b16-ft-head.test.ts:
dim is 513, not 512, and bias_index is 512. The exported graph appends a constant 1.0 to
the embedding so a fitted intercept has somewhere to live; the app's head is a bare dot
product. The probe is fitted on the post-normalisation 513-vector, because the app
normalises over head.dim and so divides that constant by the feature norm like every other
coordinate.
the rows are NOT unit norm. A text head's rows are unit norm because its readout is a
cosine; a fitted readout's row norms are the margin the fit found. They are also divided
by the temperature fitted on dataset-v2 calib, so logit_scale == temperature and the app's
softmax is the probe's own softmax (localViewScale == 1.0).
the eight nuisance prompts are intercept-only PLACEHOLDERS. They were written against the
frozen encoder's embedding space and the fine-tuned tower's features have moved off it, so
carrying the rows across would give the non-mosquito gate eight confident wrong answers.
Because bias_index is declared, informativeRows makes them invisible to the gate. Only
'a photograph without a mosquito' is a real row, fitted on this engine's own negatives.
there is no per-genus cosine calibration: PER_GENUS_COSINE_OFFSET was fitted against H/14's
embedding space and applying it here would bias the posteriors with a correction derived
from a different model.
nuisance: a photograph of an empty background
